case_name: Eğitim ve Bilim Emekçileri Sendikası v. Turkey
court: The European Court of Human Rights (Second Section)

facts.text: Eğitim-Sen, the Education and Science Workers’ Union, was formed in Ankara on 13 January 1995.

anchor.surface_text: 5.  Eğitim-Sen, the Education and Science Workers’ Union (“the union”) was forme...

facts.text: The union has 167,000 members with 90 branches and is present in 430 towns and cities.

anchor.surface_text: According to the information it has provided, the union has 167,000 members with 90 branches and is present in 430 towns and cities.

facts.text: The union is affiliated to the KESK, the Confederation of Public Sector Workers’ Union, which is a member of Education International.

anchor.surface_text: It is affiliated to the KESK (Kamu Emekçileri Sendikaları Konfederasyonu – the Confederation of Public Sector Workers’ Union), which is a member of Education International.

facts.text: On 15 September 2001 the union amended Article 2 (b) of its constitution to include the right to receive education in their mother tongue.

anchor.surface_text: 6.  On 15 September 2001 the union amended Article 2 (b) of its constitution to read as follows: “... to receive, with equality and freedom, a democratic, secular, scientific and cost-free education in their mother tongue.”

facts.text: On 15 February 2002 the Governor of Ankara requested the applicant union to delete the words “their mother tongue” from its constitution, alleging breach of Articles 3 and 42 of the Constitution and Law no. 4688.

anchor.surface_text: 7.  On 15 February 2002 the Governor of Ankara requested the applicant union to delete the words “their mother tongue” from its constitution on the ground that they were in breach of Articles 3 and 42 of the Constitution and of sections 1 and 20 of Law no. 4688 on public servants’ unions.

facts.text: The applicant union informed the Governor it was too busy but undertook to amend its constitution by 30 June 2002.

anchor.surface_text: 8.  The applicant union informed the Governor that it was too busy but that it undertook to amend its constitution by 30 June 2002.

facts.text: On 29 March 2002 the Governor of Ankara requested the public prosecutor to bring an action for dissolution against the applicant union for not amending Article 2 (b).

anchor.surface_text: 9.  On 29 March 2002, under section 37 of Law no. 4688, the Governor of Ankara requested the public prosecutor of Ankara to bring an action for dissolution against the applicant union on the ground that it had not carried out the requisite amendment of Article 2 (b) of its constitution.

facts.text: On 3 July 2002 the applicant union amended Article 2 (b) to defend the right to receive education in their mother tongue and benefit from cultural development.

anchor.surface_text: 10.  On 3 July 2002 the applicant union amended Article 2 (b) of its constitution to read as follows: “[Eğitim-Sen] defends the right of all individuals in society to receive education in their mother tongue and to benefit from the development of their culture.”

facts.text: On 16 July 2002 the public prosecutor discontinued the first dissolution proceedings due to insufficient evidence and noted the amendment of Article 2 (b).

anchor.surface_text: 11.  On 16 July 2002 the public prosecutor gave a decision discontinuing the dissolution proceedings initiated by the Governor, on grounds of insufficient evidence and incriminating factors. In his decision the public prosecutor indicated, firstly, that the applicant union had amended Article 2 (b) of its constitution, which now provided that individuals should “receive education in their mother tongue”; he further stated that the matter was being discussed in some depth both publicly and in political parties and that it would be tabled for debate in Parliament.

facts.text: On 15 October 2002 the Ministry of Labour and Social Security informed the applicant union that the amended Article 2 (b) was no longer in breach of the law.

anchor.surface_text: 12.  On 15 October 2002 the Ministry of Labour and Social Security (“the Ministry”) informed the applicant union that, following the examination of its constitution, as amended on 3 July 2002 to comply with the relevant provisions of Law no. 4688, it had been concluded that the impugned Article was no longer in breach of the law.

facts.text: On 27 June 2003 the Office of the Chief of Staff of the armed forces requested the Ministry to take measures against the applicant union for breach of Articles 3 and 42 of the Constitution due to Article 2 (b).

anchor.surface_text: 13.  On 27 June 2003 the Office of the Chief of Staff of the armed forces requested the Ministry to take the necessary measures against the applicant union on the ground that Article 2 (b) of its constitution, as amended on 3 July 2002, was in breach of Articles 3 and 42 of the Constitution.

facts.text: On 15 July 2003 the Ministry requested the Governor of Ankara to examine Article 2 (b) in light of Law no. 4688.

anchor.surface_text: 14.  On 15 July 2003 the Ministry requested the Governor of Ankara to examine the provisions of Article 2 (b) of the applicant union’s constitution in the light of section 6 of Law no. 4688.

facts.text: On 28 October 2003 the Governor of Ankara requested the applicant union to delete the words “receive education in their mother tongue” from Article 2 (b).

anchor.surface_text: 15.  On 28 October 2003 the Governor of Ankara requested the applicant union to delete the words “receive education in their mother tongue” from Article 2 (b) of its constitution.

facts.text: On 12 April 2004 the Governor applied to the public prosecutor to initiate fresh dissolution proceedings against the applicant union.

anchor.surface_text: 16.  On 12 April 2004 the Governor of Ankara, referring to the provisions of Article 2 (b) of the applicant union’s constitution and summing up the first set of proceedings against it, applied to the public prosecutor of Ankara to initiate fresh dissolution proceedings.

facts.text: On 10 July 2004 the public prosecutor brought proceedings against seven members of the executive board and requested dissolution of the union for not deleting the impugned wording.

anchor.surface_text: 17.  On 10 July 2004 the public prosecutor of Ankara brought proceedings against the seven members of the executive board of Eğitim‑Sen. In the context of that action, the prosecutor further requested the dissolution of the applicant union under section 37 of Law no. 4688 on the ground that the union had not deleted the impugned wording from its constitution.

facts.text: The Ankara Employment Tribunal assumed jurisdiction to rule on the dissolution application pursuant to Law no. 4688.

anchor.surface_text: 18.  The Ankara Employment Tribunal assumed jurisdiction to rule on the application for the dissolution of the applicant union pursuant to Law no. 4688.

facts.text: On 13 July 2004 the Ankara Employment Tribunal granted the applicant union 60 days to amend the impugned provisions of its constitution.

anchor.surface_text: 19.  On 13 July 2004 the Ankara Employment Tribunal, applying section 6 of Law no. 4688, granted the applicant union a period of sixty days to amend the impugned provisions of its constitution.

facts.text: On 15 September 2004 the Ankara Employment Tribunal dismissed the application for dissolution, finding no threat to territorial or national unity and no unlawful action by the union.

anchor.surface_text: 20.  In a judgment of 15 September 2004, the Ankara Employment Tribunal dismissed the application for dissolution. In its reasoning it indicated in particular that the relevant Articles of Eğitim-Sen’s constitution did not jeopardise (tehlike) territorial, national or State unity or the existing borders of the Republic of Turkey. It did not find that the union had committed any unlawful action capable of suggesting that the provisions of the impugned Article of Eğitim-Sen’s constitution would be used by those opposed to the unity of the Republic of Turkey.

facts.text: On 29 September 2004 the public prosecutor appealed on points of law against the tribunal's dismissal.

anchor.surface_text: 21.  On 29 September 2004 the public prosecutor appealed on points of law.

facts.text: On 3 November 2004 the Court of Cassation overturned the tribunal's judgment, ruling that dissolution was mandatory if the union did not comply within 60 days.

anchor.surface_text: 22.  In a judgment of 3 November 2004, the Court of Cassation overturned the judgment of 15 September 2004 on the ground that the Ankara Employment Tribunal had not correctly applied section 6(8) of Law no. 4688. It took the view that this section did not allow for any latitude of interpretation and that the dissolution of the union was mandatory where it had not complied with the provisions of the Law within a period of sixty days.

facts.text: On 21 February 2005 the Ankara Employment Tribunal reiterated its original findings, finding no imminent threat or incitement to violence in the union's constitution.

anchor.surface_text: 23.  In a judgment of 21 February 2005, the Ankara Employment Tribunal, contrary to the Court of Cassation’s judgment of 3 November 2004, reiterated its original findings. It referred back to the legal reasoning used in its judgment of 15 September 2004 and invoked the Strasbourg case-law on the dissolution of political parties, in particular the cases concerning the United Communist Party of Turkey and the Freedom and Democracy Party (ÖZDEP).

facts.text: On 22 May 2005 the combined divisions of the Court of Cassation quashed the tribunal's judgment and found the union's call for education in a mother tongue other than Turkish breached Articles 3 and 42 of the Constitution.

anchor.surface_text: 24.  In a judgment of 22 May 2005, the combined divisions of the Court of Cassation (Yargıtay Hukuk Genel Kurulu) quashed by a majority the judgment of the court below. In its reasoning the court indicated that Articles 10 and 11 of the Convention provided for statutory limitations to the exercise of the freedoms of expression, assembly and association and that they notably stipulated that such restrictions had to be necessary in a democratic society.

facts.text: On 3 July 2005 the applicant union amended Article 2 (b) of its constitution to remove the reference to education in mother tongue, replacing it with a general right to democratic, secular, scientific and cost-free education.

anchor.surface_text: 26.  On 3 July 2005 the applicant union amended the offending part of Article 2 (b) of its constitution to read as follows: “[Eğitim-Sen] defends, in the context of human rights and fundamental freedoms, the right of all individuals in society to receive a democratic, secular, scientific and cost-free education.”

facts.text: On 27 October 2005 the Ankara Employment Tribunal found no reason to rule on dissolution since the union had amended its constitution.

anchor.surface_text: 27.  In a judgment of 27 October 2005, the Ankara Employment Tribunal, taking note of the amendment to the union’s constitution, found that there was no longer any reason to rule on the dissolution of the union, since the material elements that had given rise to the action no longer existed.
